rv.q: Laura Wade’s incisive reworking cuts to the continually relevant themes of W Somerset Maugham’s crisp comedy of marital manners

On the basis of this witty and wise revival of The Constant Wife starring Rose Leslie as the heroine of the title, some sort of reassessment is due. In the hands of Laura Wade’s sparkling adaptation, it is a sophisticated comedy of manners stuffed with bons mots and truthful observation.

This isn’t a set-up to some fun-poking at her for her decisions; she’s the heroine of the story through and through. But thankfully, due to some excellent updating in Wade’s capable hands, it also gets a little bit deeper. What has been added in the almost-century since The Constant Wife ’s premiere is a little bit of darkness.
